# What happens in each session

Three sessions, a clinic, then Atlanta. Each session is run twice so you can take either day.

Everything is built before you travel. The weekend itself is for writing, sending and meeting people, not for setting anything up.

| | When | In the session | Your homework after it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session 1 | Mon 7 or Tue 8 September | Your Founder Brain. B2B: your sending domain | The content engine. Start collecting pictures and clips |
| Session 2 | Mon 14 or Tue 15 September | GoHighLevel and Apollo, set up and working | Your second engine, and your operations workflow |
| Session 3 | Mon 21 or Tue 22 September | Connecting your Brain to Claude | Use it. Get comfortable before you travel |
| Clinic | Wed 23 September | Your workflow loaded, and your Brain proved | Nothing. Pack |
| Atlanta | Fri 25 to Sun 27 September | Using all of it | |

Before Session 1 you only need the app running: a GitHub account, your own copy of the app, a Replit account, and a key. That is [docs/PRE-WORK.md](PRE-WORK.md), and it takes about twenty minutes.

## Session 1: your Founder Brain

The Brain is the single record of your business: what you sell, who to, what you can prove, and how you write. Everything after it reads from it, so this is the session that decides the quality of all the others.

You answer questions in your own words. It writes the file. It takes about an hour and there is no preparation.

**You choose your track here, once.** B2B if you sell to businesses, B2C if you sell to consumers. Everything after it is built for that side, and you never get asked again. If you get it wrong you can change it, and Session 1 is the cheapest time to.

### If you sell to businesses, we also set up your sending domain

This is the only thing in the programme with a hard deadline that is not ours, and it is why it is in the first session rather than a later one.

Cold email from a domain with no sending history gets filtered, whatever it says. A domain needs roughly three weeks of ordinary sending before it is trusted. Session 1 is 7 September and Atlanta is the 25th, which is eighteen days. There is no later session that works.

In the session:

1. **Set up Apollo.** The free plan is enough to start.
2. **Get a domain**, if you do not already have one that sends email regularly. You can buy it through Apollo, which is the simplest route because it connects itself and sets up the records for you.
3. **Connect the mailbox** you will send from.
4. **Check the three records**: SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Apollo can tell you whether they are actually right, rather than you hoping. Ask Claude to check them again any time before you travel.
5. **Start sending normally.** Ten to twenty real messages a day, to real people, every weekday from now until Atlanta. Ordinary email. That is what warming is.

If you already have a business domain that sends email every day, you are done in five minutes. Say so at the start.

**If you sell to consumers, none of this applies to you.** Your outreach is by hand, on Instagram, and you have no domain to warm.

### Your homework

**Build your content engine.** Say "build my content engine" in the app. It reads your Brain and writes 30 pieces in your voice. About an hour, and you can do it in pieces.

**Start collecting pictures and clips.** This is the one people leave and cannot fix on the day. The engine writes the words; it cannot film your workshop. Section 9 of the pre-work says exactly how many and what kind, split by track.

## Session 2: your tools

GoHighLevel and Apollo, set up properly, with everything connected and checked in front of you.

**GoHighLevel**, both tracks. It is your CRM, your social publishing and your automations. Buy the Starter plan in the session rather than starting a trial, because a trial started now expires during the weekend you need it.

**Apollo**, B2B only, finished off. You started it in Session 1 for the domain. Now it becomes what actually sends: your plan, your sending schedule, and your sequences.

You will connect both to your app and confirm they work. That confirmation is the point of the session: a connection that fails quietly in September is a Saturday lost in Atlanta.

### Your homework

**Your second engine.** B2B: say "build my outreach". B2C: say "build my audience engine". Your 25 messages, your sequences or your hooks and DM scripts.

**Your operations engine.** Say "build my ops engine". It finds your bottleneck, picks one GoHighLevel workflow, and writes every message inside it. You load that workflow at the clinic.

## Session 3: connecting your Brain to Claude

Up to now you have been working in the app. From here you work in Claude, and this session is the handover.

You download everything the app has made for you, open it in Claude on your own machine, and connect Apollo and GoHighLevel to your Claude account. After that, Claude can read your Brain, write in your voice, and drive both tools for you.

That is where you work from now on, and it is where you will be in Atlanta.

The steps are in [docs/WORKING-IN-CLAUDE.md](WORKING-IN-CLAUDE.md), sent before the session. Read it first if you like, but we do it together.

### Your homework

Use it. Ask it for things. Publish something. The point of the fortnight before Atlanta is that the weekend is not the first time you have done this.

## The clinic, Wednesday 23 September

Two things, and both have to be true before you travel.

**Your workflow, loaded.** You bring your operations file, load your one GoHighLevel workflow, paste your copy in, and send yourself one test through the real trigger.

**Your Brain, proved.** We check that Claude on your machine is reading your Brain and writing as you. If something is wrong with the handover, this is where it gets found, with two days to fix it rather than none.

## Atlanta, 25 to 27 September

Using all of it. Nothing here is set up on the day.

## If you fall behind

Say so in the Slack channel rather than skipping a session. Every session assumes the one before it, and a founder who arrives at Session 3 without a Brain cannot do Session 3.

Catching up is a conversation, not a problem.
